title: Wiz Flew Staff to Thailand for Five-Day Retreat With Katy Perry Concert
excerpt: CTech reported Wiz's five-day Khao Lak retreat featured a surprise Katy Perry concert estimated at $3-4 million, months after Google completed its $32 billion acquisition.
body:
• Cybersecurity firm Wiz, acquired by Google for $32 billion, flew employees to Khao Lak, Thailand, last week for a five-day vacation, CTech reported.
  • The highlight was a surprise private Katy Perry concert, estimated by CTech at about $3-4 million including her fee and production; the wider trip was estimated at tens of millions of shekels.
  • Perry's appearance drew online criticism over Wiz founders' past service in Israel's Unit 8200; Fashion Times reported Perry had not publicly responded as of November 8.
  • For customers, Dealroom notes this was a post-deal celebration, not new deal activity: Google completed the Wiz acquisition in March 2026 and Wiz sits in Google Cloud.

Wiz, the Israeli cybersecurity company Google acquired for $32 billion, flew its employees to the luxury resort area of Khao Lak in Thailand last week for a five-day vacation built around a surprise private concert by Katy Perry, according to CTech. The trip included stays at a high-end resort and a series of parties for employees.

What the celebration cost, as reported

CTech estimated the vacation at tens of millions of shekels, and Perry's private performance — fee plus production expenses — at approximately $3-4 million. Perry performed several of her hits, including "I Kissed a Girl," CTech reported, and was photographed with Wiz chief executive Assaf Rappaport. Dealroom's summary of the same CTech reporting put the figures the same way: roughly $3-4 million for the performance and tens of millions of shekels for the broader vacation.

"CTech reported that in February Wiz held its traditional Purim party at Expo Tel Aviv, themed "Wizcotheque" and estimated at about NIS 10 million, with more than 20 Israeli artists performing."

A pattern of lavish staff events

This was not a one-off. CTech reported that in February Wiz held its traditional Purim party at Expo Tel Aviv, themed "Wizcotheque" and estimated at about NIS 10 million, with more than 20 Israeli artists performing. In earlier years it flew dozens of employees to Mauritius for a private version of the reality show "Survivor," and in March 2026 it held its annual sales event in Las Vegas with a performance by Pitbull, CTech said.

Why the Perry booking drew criticism

The performance also drew criticism online. CTech reported discussion surfacing on the music forum ATRL, where users criticised Perry's decision to take part and questioned celebrities who champion social causes while accepting lucrative private bookings. Fashion Times reported the criticism centred on the company's links to former members of Israel's military intelligence: Wiz was founded in 2020 by four former Israeli military colleagues, and co-founder Assaf Rappaport served in Unit 8200. Fashion Times also noted there is no verified evidence Wiz itself operated the surveillance systems that have drawn criticism of Unit 8200, and that Perry had not publicly addressed the criticism as of November 8, 2026.

The deal behind the party

The context is the exit the party was marking. Dealroom reported Google completed its acquisition of Wiz in March 2026, after a year-long review and regulatory clearances in multiple markets, and that Wiz is now part of Google Cloud — making the Thailand retreat a post-deal celebration rather than a sign of new transaction activity.
